An exemplar is something or someone that is such a perfect, outstanding representative of a quality, category, or standard that others look to it as the model — the gold standard — of what that thing should look and feel like.

Think of it this way: out of all the examples of something that exist, an exemplar is the example. The one that captures the essence of a thing so completely and purely that it becomes the reference point for everything else.

This is the most important thing to understand about this word.

An example is simply any one instance of a thing. If you're explaining what a chair is, you can point to any chair as an example.

An exemplar, however, is not just any instance — it's the finest, most ideal, most perfectly representative instance. It's the instance that could teach someone exactly what something truly is, because it embodies that thing so completely. It carries a sense of elevation, even admiration.

A random chair is an example of furniture.
A beautifully crafted, perfectly balanced, iconic chair — one that furniture designers study and aspire to — is an exemplar of great design.

So the gap between the two words is essentially the gap between ordinary and outstanding.

1. A perfect representative of a category or quality

Here, an exemplar is something that so completely and purely represents a type of thing that it becomes the defining image of it in people's minds.

"The Eiffel Tower is an exemplar of 19th-century iron architecture."
This means: if you want to understand what great 19th-century iron architecture looks like, the Eiffel Tower is the thing to study. It captures all the essential qualities of that style at their finest.

"His career is an exemplar of quiet, determined hard work."
Meaning: his career doesn't just show hard work — it perfectly embodies it, to the point where you could hold it up and say, "This is what quiet, determined hard work truly looks like."

2. A person or thing worthy of being imitated

Here, an exemplar is a role model — someone or something so admirable in a particular quality that others are encouraged (or expected) to follow in its footsteps.

"She was an exemplar of moral courage in a time when most people stayed silent."
The person didn't just have moral courage — they demonstrated it so fully and visibly that they became a living model of what moral courage means. Others could look at her and think, "That's what I should aspire to."

"The nonprofit's transparency is an exemplar for others in the sector."
Meaning: the nonprofit's way of being transparent is so well done that other organizations should look at it and learn from it.

3. A reference sample used as a standard

This is a more specific, practical use — especially in education and professional contexts. Here, an exemplar is a sample piece of work that is shown to people so they understand exactly what a good (or sometimes bad) result looks like, so they can measure their own work against it.

"The teacher gave students three exemplars before they wrote their essays — one excellent, one average, one weak."
These aren't just random student essays. They are deliberately chosen pieces that clearly demonstrate what different levels of quality look like. Students study them to understand the standard.

"The company keeps an exemplar of each product to check new batches against during quality control."
A physical reference item — the ideal version of the product — against which every new unit is compared.

"Exemplar" is not a neutral word. It carries a tone of respect, admiration, and authority. When someone calls a person or thing an exemplar, they are saying: this deserves to be studied, followed, and held up as a model. It's a word of praise, but serious praise — the kind that comes with responsibility.

This is why you'll often see it in writing about great leaders, landmark works of art, pioneering scientific achievements, or defining moments in history. It signals that what's being talked about isn't just good — it's definitively, instructively good.

If you remember one thing...
An exemplar is the ideal model of something — so perfectly representative of a quality, type, or standard that others look to it as the benchmark. It's not just an example. It's the example.
A Few More Sentences to Cement It

• "The cathedral is considered an exemplar of Gothic architecture, studied by architects across the world."
  • "As a scientist, Marie Curie became an exemplar of perseverance and intellectual rigor."
  • "The professor handed out an exemplar of a well-structured argument so students could see exactly what was expected."
  • "This novel is not merely a good mystery story — it is an exemplar of the genre."
  • "The city's public transit system has become an exemplar for urban planners everywhere."

In each of these, you'll notice the same thing: the exemplar is something pointed at — held up, studied, and measured against. That's the soul of the word.
